Stop 1: <Mountain>

Coordinates: 10.828056, 107.882774

Type/Specialty: Natural Landmark

In 1872, Master <A>, a great sage with the Dharma name <B>, sought solitude by retreating into the wild, untouched forest of <Mountain>, a place then teeming with dangerous animals. In the late 19th century, a great sage known as Master <C>, with the Dharma name <B> and the Dharma title <A>, secluded himself in the tranquil surroundings of <Mountain>. The mountain rises 649 meters above the plain and is reached by a cable car or a forest trail. Lush greenery along the trails of the old forest. The mountain's history of solitude and faith converges here, where nature and spirituality meet in tranquil harmony. <Country> is the only country in <Region> that grows dragon fruit. You might also visit a local fruit farm on your way back.

Directions: Walk on to <Statue>.

Stop 2: <Statue>

Address: <Mountain>, <Wrong District>, <Province>, <Country>

Coordinates: 10.828056, 107.882774

Type/Specialty: Cultural Landmark

The mountain rises 649 meters above the plain and is reached by a cable car or a forest trail. The <Statue> lies on a terrace near the summit and faces east. In 1958, a monk began building the statue, which measures 49 meters in length. Pilgrims reach the terrace by a long stone stairway from the lower pagoda.

Across these stops, one thread runs through: the places that shape <Mountain> and the <Statue>. Taken together, the stops add up to more than any one of them seen alone. <Mountain> is one you might carry with you. That's 2 stops in all.
